title: [Mouse Jump] - Keyboard actions (1-9, Home, End, etc) don't appear to work after v0.101

judgment.rationale: The issue is independently reproduced by the author of the current Mouse Jump WinUI work: linked PR #50489 records that Escape and all number, numpad, Home/End, and arrow shortcuts fail after the v0.101 WinUI migration. Current main wires PreviewKeyDown only on a StackPanel and Image, then attempts to focus the Image; the XAML contains no focusable control. This is enough to pursue a focused keyboard-focus/routing fix without asking the reporter for generic logs.
evidence: The issue reports that 1-9, Home, and End no longer move the cursor in the Mouse Jump preview after v0.101.
Open PR #50489 cross-references the issue and records failed manual checks for Escape, number-row, number-pad, Home/End, and arrow shortcuts while pointer activation still works.
The WinUI migration commit e0010c56426af2722a02357e83c08a0ab2d489cb introduced PreviewWindow.xaml and PreviewWindow.xaml.cs in v0.101.
Current PreviewWindow.InitializeWindow subscribes PreviewKeyDown on StackPanel and PreviewImage, and PreviewWindow_Activated calls PreviewImage.Focus.
Current PreviewWindow.xaml contains only a StackPanel and Image and declares no focusable input control or tab stop.
Focused source review covered upstream main 71340eed47f7cf6f53b68b86a7939ad1240c3de7.
judgment.recommended_action: Prepare a focused Mouse Jump WinUI input-routing design and reproduce it on the current build; do not request another generic diagnostic archive.

fix_assessment.rationale: No linked PR fixes the keyboard regression. PR #50489 fixes preview sizing but explicitly lists these keyboard checks as failing, while current main still relies on focus and routed key events from non-interactive preview elements.

proposed_fixes.title: Give the Mouse Jump preview a reliable keyboard input target
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The WinUI preview routes key handling through a StackPanel and Image while attempting to focus the Image. After the WinUI migration, the preview can become foreground without a reliable focused XAML element, so PreviewKeyDown never reaches the handler even though its key-to-monitor logic is intact.
plan: In PreviewWindow.xaml, introduce or configure a focusable root input surface without changing pointer hit testing or the borderless overlay.
In PreviewWindow.xaml.cs, focus that surface only after the HWND is shown and activated, verify the focus call result, and centralize the key handler on the root.
Keep Escape, number row, numpad, Home/End, and Left/Right behavior unchanged once an event arrives, and add a fallback diagnostic when focus cannot be acquired.
Add focused UI coverage for keyboard activation after repeated show/hide cycles and after pointer activation.
verification: On current main, open Mouse Jump and verify Escape dismisses it and number-row, numpad, Home/End, and Left/Right keys move the pointer as documented.
Repeat activation after pointer clicks, multiple monitors, mixed DPI, and multiple show/hide cycles.
Confirm PR #50489's preview sizing and pointer-click scenarios remain unaffected.

confidence.rationale: The regression boundary, failed key set, and current focus/routed-event implementation align closely, but a local focus-state trace is still needed before choosing the exact WinUI focus primitive.

issue_context.summary: Mouse Jump's WinUI preview opens and responds to pointer interaction, but keyboard navigation and dismissal stopped working after the v0.101 migration.
known_information: The regression affects number-row, numpad, Home/End, arrow, and Escape keys according to the linked PR's current manual test matrix.
Pointer clicking still moves the cursor, so preview layout and pointer handling are not generally broken.
The current window subscribes routed PreviewKeyDown handlers on its StackPanel and Image and attempts to focus the Image on activation.
The XAML declares no focusable control in the preview.
PR #50489 is open for a separate preview-size regression and explicitly does not fix this keyboard issue.
Live upstream issue activity was reviewed through 2026-09-11T22:03:49Z.
inferences: The WinUI migration likely lost a reliable focused element or key-routing surface.
The key-to-screen selection switch is probably not the failing boundary because every handled key family fails together.
issue_context.analysis: The linked PR supplies stronger reproduction evidence than a new reporter diagnostic would: the preview is shown, mouse actions work, and every routed keyboard action fails. The shared failure boundary is focus/routing before PreviewWindow_PreviewKeyDown. A contained design should establish a focusable root and verify focus after the native show/activation sequence.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue, automated triage comment, labels, assignees, and cross-reference to PR #50489.
Read PR #50489's full validation matrix and confirmed that the keyboard failures are explicitly separated from its preview-size fix.
Inspected current PreviewWindow.xaml and PreviewWindow.xaml.cs on upstream main.
Reviewed the WinUI migration commit e0010c56426af2722a02357e83c08a0ab2d489cb, whose validation originally marked these keyboard scenarios passing.
Focused source review covered upstream main 71340eed47f7cf6f53b68b86a7939ad1240c3de7.

reproduce.title: Verify WinUI preview keyboard focus and routing
prerequisites: At least two displays or virtual displays
steps: Enable Mouse Jump on a current build with at least two displays.
Activate the preview and press Escape; reopen it after the result.
Test number-row 1-9, numpad 1-9, Home, End, Left, and Right.
Repeat after clicking the preview and after several show/hide cycles while recording which element has keyboard focus.
reproduce.expected_result: Escape dismisses the preview and each navigation key moves the pointer to the documented display without requiring a mouse click first.
reproduce.version_requirement: Current upstream main or a build containing the v0.101 WinUI migration
